items.topic: CLIP contrastive recipe: dual encoders, projection layers, InfoNCE on (image, caption) pairs
items.notes: Section 22.2.1 walks through dual encoders, projection, NxN similarity, symmetric InfoNCE with formula; matches slide content thoroughly.

items.topic: Cosine similarity background (normalized vectors equal dot product)
items.notes: Book uses cosine similarity throughout but does not include a brief recap or the 'equals dot product when normalized' identity as the slide does. A one-line aside in 22.2.1 would close the gap and help readers who skipped the math prerequisite.

items.topic: CLIP zero-shot classification by nearest text embedding
items.notes: Section 22.2.2 plus Code Fragment 22.2.1 cover the mechanism, the structure of the embedding space, and the ImageNet 75.5% number.

items.topic: OpenCLIP and sentence-transformers libraries for CLIP inference
items.notes: Book uses Hugging Face CLIPModel and discusses OpenCLIP weights in 22.2.6, but does not show the sentence-transformers wrapper that the slides use. Worth one paragraph or a code snippet showing the encoder.encode pattern for retrieval pipelines.

items.topic: Pool-from-ViT and pool-from-text-encoder internals (step-by-step)
items.notes: Book describes CLS-token pooling in ViT and EOS pooling for text but does not assemble the full 'image side, text side, project to common space, normalize, compare' walk-through that the slide deck spends 4 slides on. A diagram or a 5-step bullet list would match the slide pedagogy.

items.topic: VisualBERT: R-CNN bounding-box features, MLM + SIA training, VQA fine-tuning heads
items.notes: VisualBERT, R-CNN-based region features, Sentence-Image Alignment, and closed-vocabulary VQA classification heads are not discussed anywhere in Chapter 22. Could fit as a historical-roots note in 22.3 (pre-LLaVA VLM lineage) or in a sidebar comparing region-feature versus patch-feature visual inputs.

items.topic: Open versus closed VQA: binary classification head over (image, question, candidate-answer)
items.notes: Open-ended VQA recipe (embed image + question + candidate, binary head per candidate) is absent. Could land in 22.3 with a brief note on classical VQA evaluation versus generative VLMs.

items.topic: BLIP-2 Q-Former: learnable query vectors, cross-attention, fixed soft-token output
items.notes: Section 22.3.4 covers 32 learnable queries, cross-attention, fixed-size output, plus the full three-loss stage-1 explanation and the stage-2 projection. Diagram 22.3.2 is detailed.

items.topic: BLIP-2 Q-Former stage 1 proxy tasks: ITM, ITC, ITG
items.notes: Three losses covered with masks, hard-negative mining, and the combined-objective math. Excellent match to slide content.

items.topic: BLIP-2 stage 2: project queries into LLM token embedding space
items.notes: Section 22.3.4 explicitly describes the second stage as freezing the Q-Former and training only the projection plus an LM loss with frozen LLM.

items.topic: BLIP-2 inference: preprocess image, model.generate flow for captioning and multimodal chat
items.notes: The chapter has a LLaVA-NeXT generate() example but no BLIP-2 / BLIP-3 inference snippet. A short code fragment showing AutoProcessor + Blip2ForConditionalGeneration on a captioning task and a multi-turn chat-history pattern would balance the connector-pattern discussion.

items.topic: Taxonomy of pretrained vision model families: task-specific, representation, multimodal, generative
items.notes: Section 22.1.5 discusses pretraining objectives (supervised, MIM, contrastive, self-supervised) but does not explicitly present the four-bucket 'task-specific vs representation vs multimodal vs generative' taxonomy used to scaffold the slide deck. A short framing paragraph or a four-row table at the top of 22.1 would give readers the mental shelf the slide deck provides.

items.topic: Pretrained representation models as frozen backbones for downstream classifiers
items.notes: Section 22.1 names DINO and ResNet but does not show the classic 'freeze backbone, train linear head' workflow that 2223 spends 6 slides on. A small code snippet (requires_grad=False, AutoImageProcessor + AutoModel embedding extraction, plus a Trainer head) would help readers coming from a CV background. Could land in 22.1 or in a new appendix.

items.topic: [CLS] vs mean pooling tradeoff for ViT representations
items.notes: Section 22.1.2 mentions CLS for classification and per-patch for dense prediction but does not contrast CLS pooling with mean-pooling, which the slide highlights as producing distinct embeddings with different downstream properties. A two-line note would fill the gap.

items.topic: ViT patch tokenization: flatten 16x16x3 patch, linear projection (BPE analogy)
items.notes: Section 22.1.1 covers patch partition, flattening, linear projection (with the convolution implementation note in 22.1.5), and the LLM-to-ViT tokenization analogy in the sticky-note metaphor.

items.topic: ViT training regimes: supervised on ImageNet, MAE masked autoencoding, DINO self-distillation
items.notes: Section 22.1.5 lists supervised, MIM (MAE/BEiT), contrastive (CLIP/SigLIP), and self-supervised (DINO/DINOv2), with the MAE/DINOv2 math in the Note callout.

items.topic: ViT for classification: split, embed, add positional encoding, transformer blocks, CLS head
items.notes: Figure 22.1.1 plus the code fragment cover the full classification pipeline.

items.topic: ViTForImageClassification fine-tuning workflow with Hugging Face Trainer
items.notes: Book shows ViTModel inference but does not show a ViTForImageClassification.from_pretrained + Trainer fine-tune on a custom label vocabulary (the workflow that occupies 3 slides of 2332). Worth a short code fragment to support readers training their own classification heads.

items.topic: DeiT: data-efficient ViT via CNN-teacher distillation token
items.notes: DeiT and its distillation token (ImageNet-1K versus ImageNet-21K) are not covered in Chapter 22. Could fit in 22.1 as a sidebar on data efficiency for ViTs, or in a new sub-section on the ViT family. The pedagogy of distilling from a CNN teacher into a special token is a useful pre-cursor to DINO self-distillation.

items.topic: DINO self-distillation: local vs global crops, EMA teacher, pseudo-label SoftMax with centering
items.notes: Section 22.1.5's Note callout covers the EMA teacher and centering for DINOv2, but the original DINO local-vs-global crop strategy (96x96 local, 224x224 global, multi-crop targeting) is not described. The two-network / multi-crop intuition deserves a paragraph because it is the conceptual heart of self-distillation pretraining.

items.topic: DINOv2 attention maps: clean object-localized attention to [CLS] token
items.notes: Section 22.1.6 mentions DINOv2 segments cleanly but does not show or reference the attention-map visualization (cup, animal) that is the canonical DINOv2 figure. A figure plus one sentence interpreting it would strengthen the section.

items.topic: Swin Transformer: shifted local windows, W-MSA / SW-MSA, hierarchical 2x2 patch merging
items.notes: Swin Transformer is entirely absent from Chapter 22, despite being a foundational ViT variant for dense prediction (detection, segmentation), with its W-MSA/SW-MSA alternation and FPN-style hierarchical features. Could fit as a sub-section in 22.1 or as a comparison table row alongside ViT variants in 22.1.4. The patch-merging recipe is pedagogically valuable as a CNN-pyramid analog.

items.topic: Hierarchical ViT representations as backbones for detection and segmentation (FPN-style)
items.notes: The book briefly hints at DINOv2 features being good for segmentation but does not discuss multi-scale hierarchical representations suitable as detection/segmentation backbones (the Swin/FPN pattern). A short paragraph would tie ViT variants to dense-prediction downstream tasks.

items.topic: Multimodal embedding intuition: cat-image and word 'cat' as neighbors in shared latent space
items.notes: Big-picture section and Section 22.2.2 explicitly use this framing.

items.topic: Chatting with an image: decoder over joint embeddings, multi-turn dialog
items.notes: LLaVA generate() code fragment plus Section 22.4.6 (multi-image / interleaved inputs) cover this thoroughly.

items.topic: Soft-prompt prefixing: image-derived tokens prepended to text for LLM
items.notes: Multiple sections describe visual tokens projected into LLM embedding space and prepended to text; the LLaVA MLP recipe and Q-Former recipe both explicitly cover the soft-prompt pattern.

items.topic: Cross-attention semantics: queries say what tokens want to know, keys/values supply it
items.notes: Section 22.3.4 uses cross-attention but does not include the slide's pedagogical 'queries ask, keys/values supply' framing. Could be inserted as a 1-2 sentence reminder when introducing Q-Former queries, useful for readers who do not have transformer fundamentals fresh.

top_5_must_add.topic: Swin Transformer: shifted windows, W-MSA/SW-MSA, hierarchical patch merging
top_5_must_add.where: New sub-section in 22.1 (between 22.1.6 and 22.1.7) or a row in the ViT-zoo table

top_5_must_add.topic: DeiT: data-efficient ViT via CNN-teacher distillation token
top_5_must_add.where: New paragraph or sidebar in 22.1.5 (pretraining objectives) covering the distillation-token recipe
top_5_must_add.rationale: DeiT is the ImageNet-1K bridge that made ViTs trainable without JFT-300M; its distillation-token pattern is also pedagogically useful as a stepping stone to DINO self-distillation.

top_5_must_add.topic: VisualBERT and the R-CNN region-feature lineage of VLMs
top_5_must_add.where: Historical-roots sidebar in 22.3 (before the LLaVA recipe), or in 22.7 (early fusion variants)
top_5_must_add.rationale: VisualBERT plus MLM + SIA training is the pre-CLIP VLM lineage that the slides cover in detail; including it gives the chapter the contrast that explains why patch-token VLMs replaced region-feature VLMs.

top_5_must_add.topic: Original DINO recipe: local vs global crops, multi-crop targeting, EMA teacher
top_5_must_add.where: Expand the DINOv2 note callout in 22.1.5 to cover the original DINO multi-crop strategy
top_5_must_add.rationale: The book covers DINOv2 EMA centering but skips the local/global crop construction that is the conceptual heart of self-distillation. Two paragraphs would close the loop.

top_5_must_add.topic: Four-bucket pretrained-vision-models taxonomy (task-specific, representation, multimodal, generative)
top_5_must_add.where: Reframing paragraph or four-row table at the top of 22.1 or in chapter introduction
top_5_must_add.rationale: Slide deck 2221 uses this taxonomy as scaffolding before any specific model. The chapter would benefit from giving readers the same mental shelf so later models (CLIP, BLIP, DINO, SAM, diffusion) drop into clear buckets.
